result.topic: The Venice map for shared/map.ts: ASCII district, parser, coordinate rules, validation
result.summary: Designed a 50 x 38 cell (400 x 304 m, 8 m cells) Venice district that satisfies SPEC.md section 7 and the respawn/crate/minimap rules, and proved it with an executable validator. The main canal is a reversed S like the Canal Grande: 4 cells (32 m) wide on the straights, a 45-degree run painted 5 cells tall so every cell is inside a 3x3 water window (24 m minimum), entering at the west edge, hairpin at col 13, exiting east under a 2x4 covered bridge (new legend char R, water for physics) into a 7-cell lagoon strip plus a 5x15 bacino bulge (new legend char P for pile clusters as 2.5 m balls). Eight 1-wide side-canal networks (215 cells, 1.7 km, 31 tight bends, 19 mouths, 3 dead ends), 7 arch bridges (3 over the main canal) + 1 covered, tower 52 m from the centre on a water-edge wedge, 16 docks (every quadrant, never adjacent, each with a quay; Monte Carlo 100% of 4000 random 5-enemy layouts leave a dock >= 80 m away, mean 7.3 candidates), 24 crates (12 in the lagoon, densest 40 m cluster of 7 in the bacino, farthest crate 136 m by water from a dock). Network diameter 77 cells = 616 m (62 s at 10 m/s), which equals the Manhattan distance of the grid's opposite corners, so it cannot be shorter; the quickest west-to-lagoon crossing is 360 m = 36 s via rio N2 (the spec's "roughly 40 s"). Deliverables in the scratch folder: map.txt (38 lines of 50 chars), validate.mjs (standalone, prints ALL CHECKS PASSED), gen.mjs (painter), annotate.mjs, final.md (94 KB, with the map, annotated rendering, validator output, decisions, algorithms, edge cases, day-one tests, sources), and TypeScript ready to paste: ts/shared/map.ts (parser: Legend type, parseMap -> {width,height,cells,navigable,lagoon,lagoonEdge,lagoonCells,walls(greedy merged rects, 69 for 1082 solid cells),docks{x,z,heading},crates,bridges{x,z,orientation,length,width,kind},tower,piles}, cellAt/colOf/rowOf/cellCentre/isLagoon/isNavigable, MAP_TEXT, MAP), ts/shared/map.test.ts (vitest, 12 tests pass in 205 ms), ts/src/sim/mapPhysics.ts (Rapier cuboid/ball colliders, respawnCandidates) and ts/src/render/mapGeometry.ts (instanced placeholder district). All four TS files typecheck with the repo's exact tsconfig options plus noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters. Coordinates: origin at the centre, x = (col - W/2 + 0.5)*8, z = (row - H/2 + 0.5)*8, Y up, row 0 = north = negative z; heading = Rapier rotation angle (0 = +x, +PI/2 = +z), mesh.rotation.y = -heading, both proved by running the installed Rapier 0.21.0 and three 0.186.1. No file in the repo was created or modified.

decisions.decision: Grid 50 x 38 cells at 8 m with a full B border ring; parser is size-agnostic (>= 8 x 8)
decisions.rationale: Exactly the spec's 'about 50 x 38, 400 x 300 m'; the border ring is the physics box for free
decisions.alternatives: A separate world-bounds collider kept in step with the grid by hand

decisions.decision: Extend the legend with R (covered bridge, 2 cells deep x 4 across, water for physics) and P (pile cluster, solid ball of radius 2.5 m)
decisions.rationale: The spec needs a Rialto-style landmark and lagoon piles but gives no chars; R lets the renderer roof it, P is a cluster boats can slip around
decisions.alternatives: Encode the Rialto as '=' (renderer cannot tell it apart); a full 8 x 8 m solid P cell (a block, not poles)

decisions.decision: Main canal as a reversed S: west mouth rows 6-9, bend at col 29, 45-degree run painted 5 cells tall per column, hairpin at col 13, lower arm rows 23-26 into the bacino
decisions.rationale: 32 m on the straights, never under 24 m on the diagonal (every cell inside a 3x3 water window); the real Canal Grande is 30-90 m and is itself a reversed S; two blind corners on the lane
decisions.alternatives: 90-degree stair bends (inside corner cuts to 24 m, reads as stairs); a north-south lane (the lagoon side would then be short)

decisions.decision: Lagoon along the east edge: 7-cell strip full height plus a 5 x 15 bacino bulge at the canal mouth; lagoonEdge exported so the renderer draws that border as a breakwater
decisions.rationale: 'Open water along one edge'; 96 m of open water at the mouth is where big fights go; physics keeps the B ring
decisions.alternatives: Lagoon along the south edge under the hairpin (makes the quiet SW the hot zone and separates the covered bridge from the open water)

decisions.decision: Eight 1-wide side-canal networks; each links two thick-water places except three dead-end spurs; validator refuses any 2-wide water outside main canal and lagoon
decisions.rationale: 'One gondola fits easily, two scrape'; loops let hunters circle, nobody is forced to U-turn in 8 m; at most 4 dead ends so fleeing boats are not cornered
decisions.alternatives: 2-cell rii (16 m, ambush feel gone); more dead ends (too many traps)

decisions.decision: Walls as a greedy rectangle merge of B and T (69 rectangles for 1082 cells); piles as separate ball colliders; tower exported separately for the renderer
decisions.rationale: 69 cuboids instead of 1082 keeps the broad phase trivial and gives the art track 69 blocks; merging T is correct for physics
decisions.alternatives: Per-cell colliders (1082, visible seams); a trimesh of the water outline (hollow in Rapier, more code)

decisions.decision: Origin at the centre, row 0 = north = negative z, heading = Rapier rotation angle with forward (cos h, sin h) in (x, z), mesh.rotation.y = -heading
decisions.rationale: One rule for sim and renderer; proved by running Rapier (collider along local +x lands at (cos, sin)) and three (makeRotationY maps +x to (cos, 0, -sin))
decisions.alternatives: Row 0 at positive z (text upside down versus the top-down minimap)

decisions.decision: Dock heading = away from the quay: sum of (dock - B neighbour) vectors, best dot with an open direction, ties by water ahead then E,W,S,N
decisions.rationale: Boats spawn facing open water, dead-end docks face the exit; deterministic and covered by a test that the cell ahead is never a building
decisions.alternatives: Hand-written headings per dock (drift out of step with the text)

decisions.decision: parseMap throws MapError at import time for structural breakage; design checks (counts, widths, diameter, density, Monte Carlo) live in shared/map.test.ts; validate.mjs is the standalone design tool
decisions.rationale: A broken edit fails npm run dev and npm test in a second; the heavy checks cost ~100 ms, too much for import
decisions.alternatives: Only a test (a bad merge could reach the demo PC); everything at import (slow startup)

decisions.decision: Accept a 616 m network diameter and 512 m main-canal length while the quickest west-to-lagoon crossing is 360 m
decisions.rationale: 616 m equals the Manhattan distance between the grid's opposite corners (47 + 30 cells), so no shorter water network exists at this size; the spec's 'roughly 40 s' matches the 36 s shortcut via rio N2
decisions.alternatives: Shrinking the map or removing the far corners (loses the quiet respawn pockets the 80 m rule needs)

open_questions: The spec says 'crossable in roughly 40 s'; the shortest west-to-lagoon crossing is 36 s but the network diameter is 62 s and the main canal alone is 51 s. If the team wants the far corners closer, the only lever at 50 x 38 is to shrink the lagoon strip or the SW quarter; decide at the Gate 2 playtest.

Side-canal 'count': the spec's 'about 8' is matched by 8 connected one-wide networks, but one of them (W3+S1+S4) is a 95-cell ring. If the team wants 8 separate rii, break the S4-to-S1 link at (14,33) with a B (adds a dead end, total 4).
Whether a dock adjacent to the bacino (36,23) should count as 'in the lagoon' for the minimap reveal; the lagoon mask currently includes it. Easy to change by excluding S from LAGOON_PASS.
Bridge clearance (4 m above water) and the covered bridge roof height are placeholders for track C; the physics does not care.

Crate drift: crates are light bodies in the spec; the sim should clamp a crate back toward its cell centre when it drifts more than ~4 m so it never ends up against an abutment under a bridge. Not implemented here (sim topic).
test_ideas: Run node validate.mjs after every map edit; it must print ALL CHECKS PASSED (counts, connectivity, widths, bridges, docks, crates, diameter).
npm test with shared/map.test.ts in place: 12 design tests plus parseMap error cases (ragged line, unknown char, two water regions).

Keyboard-harness debug key M: top-down orthographic view with wall rectangles as wireframes, dock arrows along heading, crates as dots, lagoon mask tinted; verify row 0 is at the far side and no rectangle overlaps water.

Drive a box boat from dock (15,26) north: it must hit the lower arm's north wall after ~32 m and bounce; drive east under the covered bridge at x = 16 without collision; enter the rio at (22,27) and confirm the 8 m walls scrape on turns.
respawnCandidates(MAP, [{x: cell(41,24)}], 80) must exclude docks (36,23), (37,17), (38,31) and include every western dock; with enemies on all 16 docks it must still return one fallback dock.
isLagoon(MAP, 140, -100) true, isLagoon(MAP, -190, 0) false; cellAt(MAP, tower.x, tower.z) === 'T'; cellAt far outside the grid === 'B'.
Gate 2 metrics: average respawn-to-first-crate time (< 10 s), share of kills inside the lagoon mask (40-60%), count of respawns that used the fallback dock (0).
Property test for the wall merge: for random small grids, the summed rectangle area equals the solid cell count and no two rectangles overlap.

result.topic: Game rules, lobby and team logic, match flow, HUD data, keyboard harness and the tuning config (src/sim/rules.ts, teams.ts, items.ts, aim.ts, hud.ts; src/scene/layout.ts, keyboard.ts, bot.ts; shared/config.ts, shared/state.ts; tests)
result.summary: Wrote /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-makhlugjafarov-cognitex-Documents-regata-storica/69884729-7585-4b5d-ad26-4af5e194adaa/scratchpad/research/rules/final.md: the spec's words on the problem, every decision with rejected alternatives, and 14 ready-to-paste files (shared/config.ts, shared/state.ts, src/sim/{teams,rules,items,aim,hud}.ts, src/scene/{layout,keyboard,bot}.ts, tests/{teams,rules,aim,layout}.test.ts). All of it was type-checked in a scratch copy with the repo's strict tsconfig (plus noUnusedLocals/Parameters, TS 5.9.3) and 57 vitest 5.0.5 tests pass; the repo was not modified. Key results: team balancing is teams = min(6, ceil(n/size)) with sizes floor/ceil spread (table for n = 1..18 for sizes 3 and 2), a rebalance that matches the balanced multiset to current team sizes so only surplus people move (most recent unpinned joiners first; at most one existing player moves per join, proven by test); manual swap/move pins players; capacity 6 x size with a join-order spectator queue; disconnects keep the slot and the keyboard takes it. Match flow is lobby -> countdown 10 -> battle 300 -> optional overtime 30 (tied teams only, others 'out', next kill wins, else first-to-score then draw) -> results 20 -> lobby, all on absolute sim-time timers so pause = not stepping. Hit resolution order: not alive, own team, not lethal (Water Cannon, unboosted/slow ram, both boosted), spawn protection (Shield kept), Shield, sunk; mines credit the dropping team forever; timeline hit -> sinking 2 s -> respawn at 5 s -> protection to 8 s, ended by any firing including the Water Cannon (config flag); kill-cam uses the killer's pose frozen at the hit; docks need 80 m from every enemy with farthest-dock fallback; water 25/s fill, 40/s bail at full shake, 20/s auto-drain for 1-2 person teams. Aim: assist bends up to 4 deg toward the smallest-offset enemy in an 8 deg / 70 m cone, 'under crosshair' is a ray-vs-3.5 m hull circle with 4.6 m hysteresis, the 0.6 gyro gain is applied by the sim when integrating the phone's raw dYaw, Torpedo locks the nearest enemy by distance in a 40 deg cone around the aim (not the bow), Mortar within 10 deg / 60 m else 40 m ahead, and line of sight (injected callback, Rapier castRay with ONLY_FIXED) gates the diamond, the assist and the lock but not the Mortar. Split-screen rects for 2..6 teams with minimap placement and a bottom-left GL conversion for three's setViewport/setScissor; team colours Rosso #E53935, Azzurro #29B6F6, Verde #4CAF50, Oro #FFD600, Viola #BA68C8, Arancio #FB8C00 with computed WCAG contrast and min pairwise dE 42.5. Keyboard harness on KeyboardEvent.code with F1-F6 plus number-row alternatives, fullscreen + Keyboard Lock to make F-keys reliable in Chrome, and a bot that drives, loots, fires and bails so four viewports can be tested without phones. GameState is plain JSON (round-trip verified) and must never hold Rapier handles (observed as 5e-324 packed floats).

decisions.decision: Team membership lives only in teams[i].members (ordered ids); role = index; players carry no team/role field (slotOf derives it).
decisions.rationale: One source of truth; duplicated fields drift after swaps and rebalances.
decisions.alternatives: player.team / player.role fields.

decisions.decision: teams = min(6, ceil(n/size)); sizes = floor(n/t) with the first n mod t teams +1; capacity 6 x size, extra joiners queue as spectators in join order.
decisions.rationale: Matches the spec's 7 -> 3+2+2 and 12 -> 4 teams; gives a closed-form table for n = 1..18.
decisions.alternatives: Fill teams to full size and leave a remainder (3+3+1).

decisions.decision: Rebalance matches the balanced multiset to teams by current size (ties: more pinned, lower index), dissolves the smallest teams, moves unpinned most-recent joiners first, fills deficits in join order, and runs after every join/leave/size change/manual move.
decisions.rationale: Each surplus person moves exactly once, which is the minimum for the target multiset; at most one existing player moves per join (tested).
decisions.alternatives: Re-deal everyone by join order after each change (re-seats many); leave imbalance until the host presses Balance.

decisions.decision: Manual swap pins both players; manual move needs a free slot (< teamSize), pins the mover, then the balancer may bump one unpinned player from an over-full team.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the spec's balance invariant while honouring deliberate placements.
decisions.alternatives: Allow 3+3+1 after a manual move.

decisions.decision: Disconnect during countdown/battle keeps the slot; the boat idles after 1.5 s without packets; reconnect by token resumes; keyboard focus (1-6) overrides; removal only in the lobby.
decisions.rationale: Nobody's role changes mid-match; the keyboard is the spec's backup.
decisions.alternatives: Auto-remove and rebalance mid-match.

decisions.decision: Start requires at least 2 teams each with a connected Pilot; missing Enable controls or Ready is only a warning.
decisions.rationale: The keyboard can cover any phone; one stuck person must not block the room.
decisions.alternatives: Require all players ready/enabled.

decisions.decision: Overtime is its own GameState phase, mapped to 'battle' in the phone Hud; non-tied boats become status 'out' (removed, their mines/projectiles cleared); tied boats keep position and items, dead ones respawn immediately, all are minimap-revealed; still tied after 30 s -> earliest final kill wins, 0-0 -> draw.
decisions.rationale: Eliminated teams must not decide the match; 30 s is too short for hide and seek; one deterministic end.
decisions.alternatives: Repeat overtime; coin flip; keep eliminated boats as hazards.

decisions.decision: All timers are absolute sim times compared with simTime; pause = do not step; results auto-return to a rematch-ready lobby after 20 s.
decisions.rationale: No drift, pause freezes everything, tests are instant.
decisions.alternatives: setTimeout / performance.now() based timers.

decisions.decision: Hit check order: not alive, own team, not lethal, spawn protection (Shield kept), Shield, sunk.
decisions.rationale: A fresh boat must not lose a looted Shield to a shot the bubble should absorb.
decisions.alternatives: Shield before protection.

decisions.decision: Any firing ends spawn protection, Water Cannon included (config flag weapons.waterCannon.endsSpawnProtection).
decisions.rationale: The stream pushes enemies into mines and walls; the spec calls it a kill setup.
decisions.alternatives: Only lethal weapons end protection.

decisions.decision: Kill-cam follows the killer while alive and falls back to the killer's pose frozen at the hit; debug sinks show the own boat with 'SUNK'.
decisions.rationale: No cut to an empty dock when the killer sinks or respawns.
decisions.alternatives: Follow the killer entity regardless of status.

decisions.decision: Respawn dock: random among docks >= 80 m from every enemy and >= 12 m from any boat or earlier pick this step; fallback farthest-from-nearest-enemy; last resort any dock.
decisions.rationale: Spec's spawn-kill rule plus no double booking.
decisions.alternatives: Fixed per-team docks.

decisions.decision: Water: fill 25/s, bail shake x 40/s on 3-person teams (no natural drain), 20/s automatic on 1-2 person teams; speed x (1 - 0.5 w/100).
decisions.rationale: Spec's formula and 'half speed' rule; the Engineer keeps a job.
decisions.alternatives: Natural drain for everyone.

decisions.decision: Crate points have a fixed category (3 of 5 red); contents rolled by weight among enabled tiers (Cannon 50 / Torpedo 30 / Mortar 20; Shield 35 / Mine 35 / Boost 20 / Smoke 5 / Wave 5); respawn 8 s, 4 s in the last minute when stretch is on.
decisions.rationale: Gunners need weapons to score; tiers are one table.
decisions.alternatives: Random category per respawn; equal weights.

decisions.decision: Aim assist picks the smallest angular offset within 8 deg / 70 m and bends by at most 4 deg; 'under crosshair' is a ray-vs-hull-circle test (3.5 m, 4.6 m sticky) within 90 m; the 0.6 gain is applied by the sim when integrating the phone's raw dYaw.
decisions.rationale: Angular test matches what the player sees; hysteresis stops flicker; the phone cannot know about enemies and the sim is the single source of truth.
decisions.alternatives: Nearest-by-distance assist; fixed-angle crosshair test; apply the gain on the phone.

decisions.decision: Torpedo lock = nearest enemy by distance in a 40 deg cone around the AIM, within 70 m; Mortar = nearest within 10 deg / 60 m ignoring walls, else 40 m ahead along the aim.
decisions.rationale: The lock ring sits on the crosshair; a bow-relative lock could fire at an off-screen boat; homing makes distance matter more than angle.
decisions.alternatives: Lock around the bow.

decisions.decision: Line of sight (Rapier world.castRay with QueryFilterFlags.ONLY_FIXED, injected as a callback) gates the red diamond, the assist and the Torpedo lock; not the Mortar.
decisions.rationale: A diamond or lock on a boat behind a wall invites wasted shots; cost is at most 6 rays per step.
decisions.alternatives: No LOS; LOS for the Mortar too.

decisions.decision: Ranking: kills desc, deaths asc, earliest lastKillAt, index; results add topGunner (most kills by one player, any role) and bestRam (highest lethal ram impact speed).
decisions.rationale: Spec order plus a deterministic podium for places 2..6.
decisions.alternatives: Kills minus deaths.

decisions.decision: Layouts: 2 = halves, 3 = 2x2 with BR overview, 4 = 2x2 with a centred square minimap (24% of height), 5 = 3x2 with BR overview, 6 = 3x2 with a 22% centre minimap; top bar overlay x 0.28..0.72, h 7.5%; rects normalised top-left with toGlPixels for three.
decisions.rationale: Spec table; three's setViewport/setScissor use a bottom-left origin.

result.topic: 2D boat physics with Rapier 2D 0.21 and custom projectiles (src/sim/physics.ts, boat.ts, walls.ts, items.ts, projectiles.ts, loop.ts, coords.ts, geom.ts, sim.ts; PHYSICS block of shared/config.ts; tests/sim/*.test.ts)
result.summary: Researched and prototyped the whole physics layer for Gondola Royale against the installed packages. Every Rapier API claim was read from node_modules/@dimforge/rapier2d-compat/dist/**/*.d.ts and proven with node scripts (init, stepping, events, contactPair, castRay with group filters, handles, removal, query visibility, timings). The deliverable final.md (122 KB) contains: the spec's problem statement; 15 decisions with rejected alternatives; formulas (Rapier damping v*=1/(1+dt*d), terminal speed F/(m d), steering torque from the steady-state rate, keel decay, ram closing speed, slab test, mortar parabola); nine ready-to-paste TypeScript files plus the PHYSICS config block, all typechecked with the repo's strict tsconfig (plus noUnusedLocals/Parameters) in a scratch mirror; 26 edge cases with their handling; a day-one test plan with and without phones; six passing vitest files (34 tests) embedded as Appendix B; sources; and an appendix of measured numbers. Key findings a skeptic should know: (1) coordinate binding sim.y = -world.z with the bow as Rapier local +y makes simAngle identical to Object3D.rotation.y and keeps angular-velocity signs (pinned by a test against Three's own quaternion); (2) Rapier 2D 0.21 collider/body handles are opaque f64 numbers whose JS-side lookup ignores the generation, so stale handles alias newer colliders in the same slot: the design keys a Map by handle and defers removals; (3) scene queries see a new collider only after the next world.step() (propagateModifiedBodyPositionsToColliders does not help), so the static world build ends with one step; (4) sensors add mass unless density 0; (5) the compat bundle needs zero Vite config (verified vite build and dev pre-bundling), 3.4 MB / 1.3 MB gzip, loaded by dynamic import on the SCENE route only; (6) step cost is 0.13 ms for a full scene, castRay 1.2 microseconds. Thrust 10 kN with linear damping 1.0 on a 1000 kg hull gives exactly 10 m/s top speed (95 % at 3 s), boost x1.6 gives 16 m/s, hull water scales thrust. Rams are detected from collision 'started' events using velocities cached before the step plus the manifold normal and solver contact point; sinking hulls switch collision groups to a zero filter, are disabled after 2 s, and are teleported and protected on respawn.

decisions.decision: Use @dimforge/rapier2d-compat with `await RAPIER.init()` once, loaded by dynamic import on the SCENE route; no Vite plugins or optimizeDeps changes.
decisions.rationale: The compat ESM bundle inlines the wasm as base64 (init = `gC`, decodes `jg.toByteArray("AGFzbQ...")`); a scratch `vite build` produced a 3.4 MB (1.3 MB gzip) rapier chunk with zero config and the dev server pre-bundled it; the dynamic import keeps it off phones.
decisions.alternatives: @dimforge/rapier2d (needs wasm asset + top-level-await handling), vite-plugin-wasm.

decisions.decision: Coordinates: sim.x = world.x, sim.y = -world.z, simAngle === Object3D.rotation.y, bow = Rapier body local +y so forward = (-sin a, cos a).
decisions.rationale: The mirror keeps handedness, so positive Rapier angular velocity is a positive yaw (CCW from above); no sign flips; pinned by a vitest comparing with Three r186 applyQuaternion.
decisions.alternatives: y := z (yaw = -angle - PI/2 and inverted angular signs everywhere).

decisions.decision: Boat = dynamic body, roundCuboid(0.55, 2.85, 0.15) (effective 0.7 x 3.0 half extents), setMass(1000), linearDamping 1.0, angularDamping 3.0, canSleep false, no CCD; thrust derived as m*d*v_top = 10 kN; boost x1.6; hull water multiplies thrust.
decisions.rationale: Rapier damping is v *= 1/(1+dt*d) (source + measured), so terminal speed is exactly F/(m d) and 95 % is reached at 3/d = 3 s (measured 9.49 m/s at 3 s, 10.00 at 10 s); rounded corners slide over wall seams; 0.27 m per step cannot tunnel 8 m walls.
decisions.alternatives: Density-based mass; convexHull gondola outline (verified to work, inertia 2194) rejected for now because projectile OBB tests would no longer match the hull.

decisions.decision: Keel implemented by scaling the lateral velocity component each step with setLinvel: v_lat *= exp(-grip*dt), grip 8/s (1.5/s while drifting).
decisions.rationale: Exact, monotonic, frame-rate independent, cannot overshoot; measured lateral 7 -> 0.74 m/s at 0.25 s and ~0 at 1 s with no sign change.
decisions.alternatives: Counter impulse -m*v_lat*k*dt (also measured stable at 60 Hz but explicit Euler, dt-dependent, overshoots if k*dt > 1).

decisions.decision: Steering torque sized from the steady-state turn rate: tau = omega_ss * I * angularDamping with omega_ss lerped 0.5 -> 1.3 rad/s by speed, drift x1.5, angular velocity capped at 1.8 rad/s via setAngvel.
decisions.rationale: Angular damping has the same 1/(1+dt*d) form so omega_ss = tau/(I d); principalInertia() keeps it shape-agnostic; turn radius 7.7 m at top speed fits 8-10 m canals.
decisions.alternatives: Setting angular velocity directly (loses momentum feel, fights the solver during contacts).

decisions.decision: Ram detection from COLLISION_EVENTS 'started' between hulls, using velocities cached before world.step plus the normal and solver contact point from world.contactPair; rammer must be boosted, closing speed >= 7 m/s and bow facing the normal (dot >= 0.5); both qualifying -> bounce.
decisions.rationale: After the step the solver has already resolved the impact (measured pre-step 12 m/s, post-step -1.98 m/s); the manifold is readable inside the handler on the started event (normal (0,1), point (0.70,19.00)).
decisions.alternatives: CONTACT_FORCE_EVENTS with a Newton threshold (solver/mass dependent, fires on sustained pushing, no contact point in TempContactForceEvent).

decisions.decision: Sinking: collider.setCollisionGroups(SINKING member, filter 0) and keep the body dynamic 2 s with an applyImpulseAtPoint spin, then body.setEnabled(false); respawn = setEnabled(true), setTranslation, setRotation, setLinvel 0, setAngvel 0, groups PROTECTED for 3 s then BOAT; the 3D flip is render-only.
decisions.rationale: No body churn (stable handles and ids, avoids stale-handle aliasing); filter 0 removes the hull from every pair test and scene query; 2D spin is free and sells the kill-cam.
decisions.alternatives: Remove and recreate the body; kinematic body; a 3D flip in the sim.

decisions.decision: Walls: greedy row-major rectangle merge of solid map cells into cuboids on one fixed body, plus 4 border slabs, friction 0, restitution 0.4; bridge cells are water; poles ball(0.25), moored gondolas rotated cuboid(0.7,3), pile clusters 3 x ball(0.35); buildStaticWorld ends with phys.commit() (one world.step).
decisions.rationale: The spec's sample map (101 solid cells) merges into 8 rectangles; zero friction keeps scrapes from sticking; scene queries only see colliders after a step (measured).
decisions.alternatives: One collider per cell (~1000 colliders and seams); polyline contours with PolylineFlags.ORIENTED (kept as the upgrade if hulls catch on seams).

decisions.decision: Crates are solid light dynamic balls (0.8 m, 20 kg, damping 1.5) with COLLISION_EVENTS; pickup = the started event with a hull; collected crates are setEnabled(false) and re-enabled at home after 8 s.
decisions.rationale: A boat with full slots shoves the crate as the spec says, a boat with a free slot takes it on first touch; no body churn (tested).
decisions.alternatives: Sensor crates (cannot be shoved); per-step intersectionsWithShape polling (works, extra query per boat per step).

decisions.decision: Mines are one dynamic body with two colliders: solid ball(0.4) in group MINE_BODY (walls/crates only) and a sensor ball(1.6) with density 0 in MINE_TRIG (filter BOAT only, so PROTECTED hulls never trigger); arm after 1 s with a one-off intersectionPairsWith poll; 45 s lifetime; deferred removal.
decisions.rationale: Sensors generate no forces, so the solid core keeps mines out of walls; sensors add mass unless density 0 (measured 17.07 vs 10 kg); a hull already inside the sensor at arming gets no new started event (tested).
decisions.alternatives: Sensor-only mine (drifts through walls).

decisions.decision: Projectiles are plain objects: cannonball 60 m/s with per-step segment-vs-OBB (box inflated by radius) and world.castRay(ray, 1, true, undefined, Masks.queryWalls) for walls; torpedo 25 m/s pure pursuit, 120 deg/s turn cap, lock in the 40 deg cone with line of sight, straight when lost; mortar fixed 1.5 s flight to the target's launch position with no wall check and 6 m point-to-OBB splash; water cannon 18 m / 12 deg cone with LOS, addForce 6 kN and 25 water/s; own team always skipped; 4 deg aim assist within 10 deg capture.
decisions.rationale: Matches the spec's 2D rays and projectile checks; castRay costs 1.2 us; the two-way group test means query masks use membership 0xffff.
decisions.alternatives: Rapier bodies with CCD for projectiles.

decisions.decision: Fixed-step loop: accumulator, dt 1/60, 0.25 s frame clamp, prev/curr Transform2 per entity, alpha = accumulator/dt, shortest-arc angle lerp, all timers on simTime; snapshots reset on teleports.
decisions.rationale: Fix-your-timestep; clamp bounds catch-up to 15 steps; resetting prev on respawn prevents a one-frame slide across the map.
decisions.alternatives: Variable timestep (Rapier docs advise against varying dt).

decisions.decision: Entity registry is a Map keyed by collider handle with EntityRef {kind, id}; removals are deferred until the event drain finishes; no body/collider userData.
decisions.rationale: Handles are opaque f64 bit-packed values (5e-324 etc.), events report collider handles, Collider has no userData (only RigidBody does), and the JS Coarena ignores generation bits so stale handles alias newer colliders (measured).
decisions.alternatives: RigidBody.userData (typed unknown, bodies not colliders); arrays indexed by handle (impossible).

decisions.decision: Steering angle = atan2(up.x, up.y) of the low-passed (80 ms) gravity vector minus the calibrated angle, wrapped to (-180, 180]; dead zone 4 deg, full lock 35 deg, curve 0.6x + 0.4x^3; hold the last steer and grey the wheel when the in-plane gravity is below 0.35 g.
decisions.rationale: Turning the wheel is a rotation about the screen normal, which rotates the in-plane gravity components by exactly the wheel angle at any constant pitch; both landscape sides only change the calibration offset (+90/-90) and the iOS sign inversion shifts both angles by 180, so the difference is unchanged. Verified with rotation matrices (check_math.mjs) for both platforms, both landscapes, pitch 0/30/60.
decisions.alternatives: deviceorientation beta/gamma (gimbal lock exactly at the upright pose, as the spec warns); asin(up.y) elevation of the long axis (sign flips between the two landscapes, not absorbable by an offset); raw per-event angle without a low-pass.

decisions.decision: Gunner yaw rate = rotationRate . unit(up) with rotationRate = (alpha, beta, gamma) as rates about device x, y, z; soft dead zone 2 deg/s, clamp 600 deg/s, gain 2, dYaw accumulated in radians between sends.
decisions.rationale: Projecting body angular velocity on the world vertical gives the yaw rate at any tilt (checked numerically to 1e-12). The axis mapping alpha=x, beta=y, gamma=z is what the current W3C text, Chromium (RadToDeg(gyro.x,y,z) into Create(alpha,beta,gamma)) and WebKit (rad2deg(rotationRate.x,y,z) into RotationRate::create) all do; the 'alpha about z' reading is the pre-2019 spec that never matched a browser.
decisions.alternatives: rotationRate.alpha or .gamma alone (wrong unless the phone is exactly upright or flat); deviceorientation.alpha deltas as primary (gimbal lock near upright, drift, relative on iOS); Generic Sensor Gyroscope (not in Safari).

decisions.decision: Normalise gravity before projecting: up = sign * accelerationIncludingGravity, sign guessed from UA/vendor (iOS-like => -1), corrected by a GravitySignDetector that votes sign(ag.y) == sign(sin beta) during the portrait lobby (locks after 45 agreeing samples), and a persisted 'Invert aim' toggle (localStorage gr.invertAim) on top.
decisions.rationale: WebKit computes (userAcceleration + gravity) * 9.80665 unnegated from CoreMotion, so iOS reports -9.81 flat face-up while the spec and Chrome report +9.81; an un-normalised projection flips sign on iOS. The detector makes the sign independent of UA sniffing; the toggle is the last resort for an unknown sensor stack.
decisions.alternatives: typeof DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission === 'function' as the iOS test (Chrome 151 ships the same static); 'flip it after the first test' only (18 players bring both platforms).

decisions.decision: dt from performance.now() deltas clamped to [0, 100 ms] (first sample 1/60); event.interval is never read.
decisions.rationale: WebKit passes kMotionUpdateInterval = 1/60 seconds straight into the event; Chromium passes kDefaultPumpDelayMicroseconds / 1000 = 16 (integer ms). Same field, different units.
decisions.alternatives: event.interval with a unit heuristic.

decisions.decision: One ControllerPipeline keeps filtered state; a separate 30 Hz setTimeout loop on an absolute schedule samples it, builds one InputPacket with seq, latches sub-tick FIRE taps so fire=true is sent at least once, reports recenter/use edges once, and on a hidden tab sends one neutral packet, stops, then resets filters and restarts on return.
decisions.rationale: The spec says 30 Hz not per event; 60 Hz events through a tunnel double packets for nothing; sensors stop while hidden (spec) and timers are throttled, so coasting the boat immediately is the safe behaviour; the absolute schedule avoids drift and bursts.
decisions.alternatives: Per-event sends; requestAnimationFrame (throttled in background, tied to display rate); plain setInterval (drifts, bursts after a hiccup).

decisions.decision: Pads use pointer events on one root; a pointer keeps the zone it went down on; touch uses implicit capture, mouse gets setPointerCapture; CSS touch-action: none, user-select: none, -webkit-touch-callout: none, overscroll-behavior: none, 100dvh with 100vh fallback, position: fixed, safe-area padding; plus non-passive touchstart/touchmove/touchend and gesturestart preventDefault and contextmenu cancelled; releaseAll on blur, hidden and pointercancel.
decisions.rationale: Multi-touch and the desktop mouse share one code path; iOS ignores user-scalable=no and WebKit still double-tap-zooms positioned elements with touch-action: none (bug 218015), so the touch-event preventDefaults are needed; overscroll-behavior kills Chrome pull-to-refresh and Safari rubber band; dvh fixes the Safari toolbar.
decisions.alternatives: Touch events only (no mouse for the simulator); zone by current finger position (sliding across the middle flips GAS/BRAKE); click events (350 ms iOS delay, no multi-touch).

decisions.decision: Enable-controls tap starts requestFullscreen (Android), DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission (when present on any platform) and navigator.wakeLock.request synchronously before any await; DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission is not called; a 1 s (PHONE.motionWatchdogSec) watchdog reports no-events/stalled with player-facing messages for insecure, denied, needs-gesture, unsupported.
decisions.rationale: WebKit rejects NotAllowedError without a processing user gesture; one WebKit permission state covers motion and orientation and a grant starts both listeners; on http WebKit resolves denied with 'Browsing context is not secure' and Chrome 76+ never fires, so isSecureContext is checked first and the watchdog catches the rest.
decisions.alternatives: Awaiting the permission before requesting fullscreen (may lose the activation); calling both requestPermission statics (second prompt risk, no benefit).

decisions.decision: WakeLockKeeper re-requests on visibilitychange and tracks the release event; iOS below 16.4 gets a 'turn off Auto-Lock' banner; haptic() uses navigator.vibrate and falls back to a red flash when vibrate is missing or returns false; orientation via screen.orientation.type when present else matchMedia('(orientation: landscape)'); screen.orientation.lock('landscape') attempted after fullscreen on Android only.
decisions.rationale: Browsers release the lock when the page is hidden; wake lock is Safari 16.4+ (full on iOS 18.4, partial 16.4-18.3 not in Home Screen apps); Safari has no vibrate and no lock(); iPhone has no element fullscreen (WebKit 212934 WONTFIX); lib.dom 5.9 declares unlock() but not lock().
decisions.alternatives: NoSleep-style hidden video for iOS 16.0-16.3 (extra asset and autoplay rules).

decisions.decision: Shake = peaks of |linear acceleration| >= 15 m/s^2 with 120 ms refractory and 8 m/s^2 re-arm, counted over a 1 s window, 4 peaks = 1.0; when acceleration is null use ag minus a 0.5 s low-passed gravity.
decisions.rationale: Peaks per second is the spec's definition and is sign-agnostic (magnitude only); Chrome Android can report acceleration with null fields when there is no linear-acceleration sensor.
decisions.alternatives: RMS/energy (slow waving would count as bailing).

decisions.decision: Desktop simulator (KeyboardSensorSource) synthesises devicemotion and deviceorientation samples from a virtual pose with the same frames and the iOS/Android sign switch (I), no-gyro mode (N), landscape side (L); the no-gyro fallback uses the heading of the device aim axis from the full alpha/beta/gamma rotation matrix (continuous across beta = 90) with 360 wrap, and webkitCompassHeading (360 - heading) only when alpha is null.
decisions.rationale: The whole pipeline, not just the UI, runs on a laptop before the first iPhone arrives; a matrix-derived heading does not jump where raw alpha does.

claims.claim: WebKit keeps a single DeviceOrientationOrMotionPermissionState per origin (m_accessStatePerOrigin) for both motion and orientation, never prompts again once the state is not Prompt (cached across reloads, UI-process lifetime), passes mayPrompt = UserGestureIndicator::processingUserGesture, and on Granted starts both the orientation and the motion listeners.
claims.evidence: WebFetch of WebKit raw DeviceOrientationAndMotionAccessController.cpp; Apple forum thread 128376 reports the decision persisting across reloads.

claims.claim: WebKit DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission(): no page -> InvalidStateError; isAllowedToUseDeviceMotion false -> console warning 'Call to requestPermission() failed, reason: <msg>.' and resolves 'denied' (msg 'Browsing context is not secure' on http, 'API is disabled', or the Feature-Policy iframe message); state still Prompt without a gesture -> rejects NotAllowedError 'Requesting device motion access requires a user gesture to prompt'.
claims.evidence: WebFetch of WebKit raw DeviceMotionEvent.cpp and LocalDOMWindow.cpp (isAllowedToUseDeviceMotionOrOrientation).

claims.claim: The spec defines requestPermission() static methods on both DeviceOrientationEvent and DeviceMotionEvent returning Promise<PermissionState>, marks the interfaces [SecureContext], requires transient activation only when a prompt would be shown, and uses the same accelerometer/gyroscope permissions for both.
claims.evidence: WebFetch of the W3C spec (permission sections).

claims.evidence: https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-76-deps-rems/ quotes 'Chrome now restricts the API to secure browsing contexts.'

test_ideas: npm test: sensorMath.test.ts covers wrapDeg, softDeadZone, rollAngleDeg poses, steerCurve (19.5 -> 0.35, 35 -> 1, expo 0 -> 0.5), clockwise 20 deg -> +20 in both landscapes, iOS sign invariance, pitch invariance at 30/55 deg, weak pose at pitch 75, yaw projection (30 deg/s, 0 when perpendicular, sign flips with up, null for zero up), yawStepRad (1.5 -> 0; 32 -> 2*30*pi/180/60; clamp 600), 45 deg/s for 1 s -> 2*43 deg, upFromOrientation vectors, aimHeadingDeg continuity across beta 89/91, shake peaks (refractory, re-arm, 4 peaks -> 1.0, decay, gentle motion 0), GravitySignDetector +1/-1/null, low-pass step 0.5, simulator sign conventions, packet building with seq and sub-tick FIRE latch, neutralPacket.

Desktop: open /play?room=TEST&sim=1; A/D roll (eased to +/-35), W/S pitch, arrows yaw at 90 deg/s, Space shake, I flips the simulated platform sign (steer and yaw must not change), N removes the gyro (yaw source flips to 'orientation' and arrows still turn), L swaps landscape side (recalibrate, right turn still positive), mouse drives the pads; watch the relay log for a steady 30 packets/s; switch tabs and confirm exactly one neutral packet then silence; keep check_math.mjs as the independent matrix check.

Gate 1 on phones through the tunnel: iPhone prompt appears once and Allow works; debug line shows 'ag=-up (iOS)' on iPhone and 'ag=+up' on Android plus 'yaw:gyro'; negative test over http://<lan-ip>:5173 shows the 'not on https' message; Don't Allow once, read the recovery message, close tab, rejoin.

Pilot: calibrate in landscape, clockwise turn -> wheel fill grows right and the box boat turns right; 4 deg nothing, 35 deg full lock; flat phone greys the wheel and holds steer; other landscape side after recalibration behaves the same; pitch the phone 30 deg down and repeat.

Gunner: calibrate pointing at the screen, turn the body 45 deg left -> view turns 90 deg left on both phones; if reversed on one model flip Invert aim and note the model; repeat with the phone pitched 30 deg; stand still 30 s for zero drift; RECENTER snaps to the bow; quick FIRE tap registers exactly once, hold auto-fires only with an auto weapon; Android vibrates, iPhone flashes red.
Engineer: 2 s of shaking empties the meter, slow waving does nothing; portrait and landscape both work.
Lock and unlock the iPhone, background and return on Android: watchdog shows 'stalled' for at most 1 s then recovers without a prompt; screens do not dim during a 5-minute round (wake lock re-armed).

Gestures on the pads: pinch, double-tap, long-press, edge back-swipe and pull-down must do nothing; rotate to portrait shows the overlay and back to landscape hides it; the Safari toolbar never covers GAS/FIRE (100dvh).
